text: Fill in the missing terms about inborn errors of amino acid metabolism.
questions: In PKU, the cofactor *tetrahydrobiopterin/BH4:This pterin cofactor is also needed by tyrosine hydroxylase and tryptophan hydroxylase.* is required by phenylalanine hydroxylase, and its deficiency can mimic classical PKU.
The urine of an untreated PKU patient has a characteristic *musty/mousy* odour associated with phenylacetate.
In alkaptonuria, deposition of oxidised homogentisate in cartilage causes a blue-black discolouration called *ochronosis*.
Classical homocystinuria features *downward* lens dislocation, distinguishing it from the upward dislocation in Marfan syndrome.
Hartnup disease impairs neutral amino acid absorption, causing a pellagra-like rash that responds to *nicotinamide*.

overallFeedback.feedback: Each inborn error has a signature defect and clinical finding: PKU (BH4-dependent hydroxylase; phenylalanine is diverted to phenylpyruvate and phenylacetate, the latter giving the musty urine odour), alkaptonuria (ochronosis from homogentisate deposition), homocystinuria (downward lens dislocation, unlike Marfan's upward), and Hartnup disease (tryptophan malabsorption depletes niacin, treatable with nicotinamide).
